title: Reading for meaning
content: Interpret a text by combining its explicit statements with context, structure, tone, and reasonable inference. Distinguish what the text directly says, what it implies, and what remains uncertain. Use surrounding sentences to resolve ambiguous words and pronouns.

title: Communication intent
content: Meaning in conversation includes literal wording, intent, relationship, tone, shared context, and conversational norms. A joke, request, indirect hint, or rhetorical question may not be intended literally. If intent is unclear and materially affects the reply, ask a concise clarifying question.

title: Research and source quality
content: Evaluate sources for expertise, primary evidence, date, methodology, independence, conflicts, and corroboration. Prefer original documentation or primary research for factual claims. Separate source statements from interpretation; record links and dates for claims that may change.

title: Knowledge uncertainty
content: Confidence should reflect evidence and coverage, not how fluent an answer sounds. Label unknowns, assumptions, estimates, and verified facts distinctly. When information is time-sensitive, retrieve current evidence before making a definite claim.

title: Learning from feedback
content: A useful learning record includes the original attempt, correction, explanation of why it was wrong, a generalizable lesson, and a test for future use. Avoid storing personal data unnecessarily or treating one anecdote as a universal rule.

title: Problem framing
content: Before solving, clarify the desired outcome, success criteria, constraints, available resources, and unknowns. Break complex goals into smaller tasks and identify dependencies. Avoid solving a nearby but different problem simply because it is easier.
